# laravel_cloud_environment_internal_networking (Resource)

Turns on internal networking for an environment, so other environments on the same dedicated cluster can reach it over the private network at its internal hostname. Private Cloud only: the organization needs the internal networking entitlement and the environment must run on a dedicated cluster. Destroying this resource turns internal networking off.

~> **Beta:** This provider is in beta and may change between releases.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Let only the API environment reach the backend over the private network.
resource "laravel_cloud_environment_internal_networking" "backend" {
  environment_id  = laravel_cloud_environment.backend.id
  access_level    = "specific"
  environment_ids = [laravel_cloud_environment.api.id]
}

# The API reaches the backend at this hostname.
output "backend_internal_hostname" {
  value = laravel_cloud_environment_internal_networking.backend.hostname
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `access_level` (String) Which environments can send internal traffic to this one: `all` environments on the same cluster, or only the `specific` ones in environment_ids.
- `environment_id` (String) ID of an environment on a dedicated cluster. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `environment_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the environments that can send internal traffic to this one. Required with access_level `specific`, and not allowed with `all`. Each must be another environment of the organization on the same cluster.

### Read-Only

- `hostname` (String) The private hostname other environments use to reach this one.
- `id` (String) The environment ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Internal networking is imported by environment ID.
terraform import laravel_cloud_environment_internal_networking.example env-...
```
